summary: Laurentios Myriantheus was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Rizarios Ecclesiastical School and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Munich, studying under Martin Haug and Wilhelm von Christ.

Laurie L. Patton works in Indology and religious studies, holding degrees from Harvard (BA) and the University of Chicago (PhD). She served as a professor at Emory and Duke, president of Middlebury College (2015–2024), and president of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (2024).
Lavanya V. Eswar is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. As of 2026, she is a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the doctoral supervision of V. Yamuna Devi.

Lawrence Cohen, active in Indology and other fields, earned a Doctor of Pharmacy from USC (1979). He served as professor and department chair at Washington State University (2002–2012), professor at UNT Health Science Center (2021), and professor and chair at UC Berkeley (attested 2026).

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a scholar of religious studies and history and archaeology. He served as a director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and as a theology professor at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence Epstein is a Tibetologist who earned a BS from UCLA, an MD from George Washington University, and trained at VA West Los Angeles and Cedars-Sinai. He was an assistant professor at the University of Washington (attested 1999–2001).

Lawrence Heyworth Mills was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological scholar who studied at NYU, Virginia Theological Seminary, University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and Oxford (M.A., 1888). He became a professor at the University of Oxford in 1897.
Lawrence J. McCrea is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics who studied under Sheldon Pollock. He serves as a professor at Cornell University (attested 2026).

Lawrence William Nelson specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at multiple institutions, including Butler, Indiana University Bloomington, NYU, Northwestern, St. John's College, and earned a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion from the California Institute of Integral Studies.
Laxmanshastri Joshi was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Kevalananda Saraswati (~1916–1925) and served as director of Prajna Pathashala from ~1955 to 1994.
Laxmidhar Behera is a scholar in computational fields and Indology. He has held academic posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur and the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi.

Lazăr Șăineanu was a linguist who earned an M.A. from Bucharest and a Ph.D. from Leipzig. He studied under Georgian, Haşdeu, Paris, Bréal, Bergaigne, Brugmann, and Leskien, later acting for Haşdeu at the University of Bucharest (1890–1892).
LeRoy Carr Barret worked in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Washington and Lee University (~1895–1898) and at Johns Hopkins University (~1899–1903) under Maurice Bloomfield.

LeRoy Carr Barrett was an Indologist who studied at Washington and Lee and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Princeton, Dartmouth, and Trinity College, where he was professor of Latin from 1910.

Leah Judith Zahler worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia, where she studied under Jeffrey Hopkins, and also studied under Harvey B. Aronson, Joe Bransford Wilson, and Geshe Wangyal.

Lee Jonathan Chilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed an MPhil at the University of Sydney (2002–2024), where he was an alumni and executive member in 1998, and also studied at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Lee Ling Ting is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a BA from the University of Adelaide, an MA from Peking University, and a PhD from Harvard University, later serving as a postdoctoral fellow at Vassar College in 2024.

Lee Yearley specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and sinology. He held appointments at Stanford University as a professor (attested 1989–1992) and later as emeritus professor (attested 2026).

Leedom Lefferts is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. In 2011, he was attested as professor of anthropology, emeritus, at Drew University and research associate in anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.

Leela Aditi Wood specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
